places.title: Nyhavn and Kongens Nytorv
places.why: A short canal dug from the harbour to the King’s New Square, lined with tall gabled townhouses painted ochre, red and blue and moored with old wooden ships. At its head lies Kongens Nytorv, the largest square of the old city, framed by the Royal Theatre and Charlottenborg.

places.title: Tivoli Gardens
places.why: One of the oldest amusement parks in the world, laid out on the old city ramparts: a lake left from the moat, flower gardens, a Moorish palace, a Chinese pagoda and a wooden roller coaster from 1914, all lit with thousands of bulbs at night.

places.title: Amalienborg, Frederiksstaden and the Marble Church
places.architect: Nicolai Eigtved (Frederiksstaden, Amalienborg); Ferdinand Meldahl (Marble Church)
places.why: A rococo district planned on a grid around an octagonal square with four identical palaces, home of the royal family, and an equestrian statue at the centre. The axis runs from the harbour across the square to the green copper dome of the Marble Church.

photos.file: Frederik V statue in Amalienborg Palace Copenhagen 2014 02.jpg
photos.author: Julian Herzog ( Website )

places.title: Strøget
places.why: A chain of old streets and squares from City Hall Square to Kongens Nytorv, closed to cars in 1962 and one of the first and longest pedestrian streets in Europe. It passes Gammeltorv and Amagertorv with their fountains and Dutch Renaissance gables.

photos.file: Amagers torg København - Copenhagen april 17 a.jpg
photos.author: Øyvind Holmstad

places.title: Rundetårn (Round Tower)
places.architect: Hans van Steenwinckel the Younger and Leonhard Blasius
places.why: A brick observatory tower built for Christian IV with no stairs: a spiral ramp of seven and a half turns, wide enough for a horse and carriage, climbs to a platform over the rooftops of the old town.

places.title: Rosenborg Castle and Kongens Have
places.architect: Christian IV, Bertel Lange and Hans van Steenwinckel the Younger
places.why: A Dutch Renaissance summer palace of red brick and sandstone with spired towers, standing in the King’s Garden, the oldest royal garden in Denmark and the most used park in the city, with straight lime avenues, a rose garden and wide lawns.

places.title: Freetown Christiania
places.why: A self-governing community founded by squatters in 1971 in a former naval barracks on the old ramparts. Beyond the main street, hand-built houses of timber, glass and salvaged materials stand along the lakes of the fortification.

places.title: Christianshavn and the Church of Our Saviour
places.architect: Lambert van Haven (church); Lauritz de Thurah (spire)
places.why: A planned Renaissance town on reclaimed islands, crossed by a canal with houseboats and old merchant houses. Above it rises the baroque Church of Our Saviour, whose black and gold spire has an outside staircase spiralling to the top.

places.title: Christiansborg Palace and Slotsholmen
places.why: The island where Copenhagen began, now home to parliament, the supreme court and the prime minister’s office in a granite-clad palace with the tallest tower in the city. Around it stand the riding ground, the palace chapel and the old ministries.

places.title: Kastellet, the Gefion Fountain and the Little Mermaid
places.architect: Henrik Rüse (fortress); Anders Bundgaard (fountain); Edvard Eriksen (statue)
places.why: A five-pointed star fortress with grassy ramparts, moats and rows of red barracks, still in military use and open as a park. On the harbour side stand the Gefion Fountain, with a goddess driving four oxen, and the small bronze Little Mermaid on her rock.
places.note: The Little Mermaid is protected by copyright until 2029, so no photo shows it.

places.title: Jægersborg Dyrehave and the Hermitage
places.why: A royal hunting forest of old oaks and open grassland with thousands of free-roaming deer, laid out with straight hunting rides in a star pattern. In the middle of the plain stands the Hermitage, a small baroque hunting lodge.

places.title: Refshaleøen
places.why: The island of the former Burmeister & Wain shipyard, where vast workshop halls now hold an art centre, a street food market, studios and restaurants, with harbour swimming and views across to the city.
places.note: The outline is OpenStreetMap’s whole peninsula, including the Lynetten treatment plant to the north-east.

places.title: Torvehallerne and Israels Plads
places.architect: Hans Peter Hagens (market halls); COBE and Sweco Architects (square)
places.why: Two glass and steel market halls on the site of the old vegetable market, with an open-air fruit market between them. Next to them Israels Plads was rebuilt over an underground car park as a raised square for sport, play and sitting in the sun.

places.title: Assistens Cemetery
places.why: An 18th-century cemetery with tree-lined avenues and old gravestones, where Hans Christian Andersen and Søren Kierkegaard are buried. Locals use it as a park to walk, read and picnic.

photos.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thue assumed (based on copyright claims).

photos.file: Graves of Søren Kierkegaard and his family.jpg
photos.author: OleNeitzel

places.title: Botanical Garden
places.why: A ten-hectare garden on the old city ramparts with a lake left from the moat, a rock garden and a complex of glasshouses from 1874, inspired by the Crystal Palace. At its centre the 16-metre Palm House has cast-iron spiral stairs up to a walkway under the roof.

photos.file: View of the Botanical Garden, Copenhagen.jpg
photos.author: GoEThe

photos.file: University of Copenhagen Botanical Garden - DSC07653.JPG
photos.author: Daderot

places.title: The Black Diamond (Royal Danish Library)
places.why: An extension of the Royal Library on the waterfront: a leaning block clad in polished black granite from Zimbabwe, split by a glass atrium, linked to the old library by bridges over the road.

photos.file: The Black Diamond Royal Danish Library Copenhagen Slotsholmen 2014 01.jpg
photos.author: Julian Herzog ( Website )

places.title: Copenhagen Opera House
places.why: An opera house on the island of Holmen under a flat roof cantilevered 32 metres over the water, on the axis of Amalienborg and the Marble Church across the harbour. The glass foyer wraps around a maple-clad auditorium.

places.title: Royal Danish Playhouse
places.why: A theatre built partly out over the harbour: a dark brick stage tower, a glass upper storey in coloured glass and a public boardwalk of oak around the building at water level.

places.title: BLOX and the Danish Architecture Centre
places.why: A stack of glass boxes on the harbourfront that bridges a busy road and holds the Danish Architecture Centre, offices, flats and a playground, with a public route through and around the building.

photos.file: BLOX the Building Danish Architecture Center.jpg
photos.author: kallerna

places.title: DR Koncerthuset
places.why: A concert hall for the Danish broadcaster wrapped in a translucent blue screen that shows images at night. Inside the cube the main hall is a terraced vineyard of seating in red-brown wood.

photos.file: Jean nouvel, danish radio concert hall, copenhagen 2002-2009 (3551308148).jpg
photos.author: seier+seier

places.title: Axel Towers
places.why: Five round towers of different heights clad in tombac and glass fins, joined at the base around a public plaza with a stepped green roof, opposite Tivoli.

places.title: Mærsk Tower
places.why: A 15-storey research tower for the university’s health faculty, wrapped in 3,300 copper shutters, a third of which move with the sun. Around it a 300-metre raised walkway crosses the campus gardens between Nørre Allé and Blegdamsvej.

places.title: National Museum of Denmark (Prince’s Mansion)
places.why: The country’s museum of cultural history in the Prince’s Mansion, one of the few rococo town palaces in Copenhagen: a modest gate on the canal leads to a courtyard framed by four wings with original floors and halls.

photos.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

places.title: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.architect: Vilhelm Dahlerup, Hack Kampmann; Henning Larsen (extension)
places.why: A museum of ancient and French art founded by the brewer Carl Jacobsen, built of red brick and marble around a domed winter garden of palms. Henning Larsen added a gallery building for the French collection in a courtyard.

places.title: Statens Museum for Kunst (National Gallery)
places.architect: Vilhelm Dahlerup and Georg E.W. Møller; C.F. Møller (extension)
places.why: The national gallery in an Italian Renaissance revival palace on the park of the old ramparts. Behind it a long white extension opens to the park through a glass wall and a street-like hall between old and new.

photos.file: København Statens Museum for Kunst (Denmark's National Gallery).jpg
photos.author: JRodSilva

places.title: Designmuseum Danmark
places.architect: Nicolai Eigtved and Lauritz de Thurah; Kaare Klint and Ivar Bentsen (conversion)
places.why: Danish design shown in the former Frederiks Hospital, a rococo hospital around a garden courtyard, converted to a museum in 1926 by Kaare Klint, whose plain galleries became a model of Danish modernism.

photos.file: Design Museum Denmark - Bredgade view out.jpg
photos.author: lglazier618

places.title: Thorvaldsens Museum
places.why: The first museum building in Denmark, made for the sculptor Bertel Thorvaldsen: an ochre temple with painted ceilings in strong colours and an outside frieze showing the arrival of his works by ship.

places.title: Copenhagen City Hall and City Hall Square
places.why: A red-brick town hall in National Romantic style, inspired by Siena, with a 105-metre tower, a glass-roofed great hall and carved details of Nordic legends. It faces the large square at the start of Strøget.

photos.file: Windows of City Hall In Copenhagen.jpg
photos.author: John Samuel

places.title: Church of Our Lady (Copenhagen Cathedral)
places.why: The cathedral rebuilt after the British bombardment of 1807 as a severe neoclassical basilica with a portico and a coffered barrel vault, lined with Thorvaldsen’s marble statues of Christ and the apostles.

places.title: Museum of Danish Resistance
places.why: A museum partly sunk into Churchill Park: low brick volumes split by a sloping cut, with exhibitions below ground and a roofscape that becomes part of the park.

places.title: Grundtvig’s Church
places.architect: Peder Vilhelm Jensen-Klint; completed by Kaare Klint
places.why: A memorial church built over 19 years from millions of hand-finished yellow bricks, its west front a giant stepped gable like an organ. The nave is a tall brick space with pointed vaults and almost no decoration.

places.title: Bagsværd Church
places.why: A plain white church outside, like a farm building of precast panels and corrugated roofs. Inside, a concrete ceiling of rolling waves takes daylight down from high windows into the nave.

photos.file: Jørn Utzon (1918-2008) - Bagsværd Church (1976) - Zealand - Denmark - Flickr - Cederskjold Photo.jpg
photos.author: Jens Cederskjold from København S, Danmark

places.title: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
places.why: A museum of modern art that grew from a 19th-century villa into a chain of low white pavilions linked by glass corridors, set in a sculpture park sloping down to the Øresund.

photos.file: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art Pauserum.jpg
photos.author: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art / Kim Hansen

photos.file: View from the Louisiana museum lawn.jpg
photos.author: TimBray

places.title: Ordrupgaard and Finn Juhl’s House
places.architect: Gotfred Tvede; Zaha Hadid Architects; Snøhetta; Finn Juhl
places.why: An art museum in a country villa with a flowing black lava concrete wing by Zaha Hadid and an underground gallery by Snøhetta. In the garden stands the furniture designer Finn Juhl’s own modernist house, kept with his interiors.

places.title: SAS Royal Hotel
places.why: Copenhagen’s first skyscraper: a slim slab of green-grey glass curtain wall on a low base, designed down to the door handles and cutlery, for which Jacobsen created the Egg and Swan chairs.

places.title: Radiohuset
places.why: The former Danish broadcasting house, a functionalist complex of offices and studios around a fan-shaped concert hall with wood-panelled walls, now home to the Royal Danish Academy of Music.

places.title: Danmarks Nationalbank
places.why: Jacobsen’s last major work: a closed box of Norwegian marble with long bands of glass, set back behind a walled garden, with a lobby hall of marble rising the full height of the building.

photos.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thue assumed (based on copyright claims).

places.title: Skovshoved Petrol Station
places.why: A white tiled kiosk on the coast road under a round concrete canopy on a single column, like a mushroom, still selling fuel.

photos.file: PHOTO SKOVSHOVED PETROL STATION Copenhagen 1936 Arne Jacobsen 11.jpg
photos.author: Madeira78

places.title: Bellevue: Bellavista, Bellevue Theatre and Bellevue Beach
places.why: A seaside resort designed by the young Arne Jacobsen: white stepped housing with sea-view balconies, a theatre with a sliding roof, and a bathing beach with his striped lifeguard towers and kiosks.

places.title: Thoravej 29
places.why: A concrete factory of 1967 turned into a house of studios, food and community, keeping almost all of the old material on site: the raw frame, the patched floors and the cut openings are left visible.

places.title: Centre for Health
places.why: A health centre for people living with type 2 diabetes, built around a hall of 15-metre timber arches, with a sports hall, studios and a teaching kitchen in warm exposed wood.

places.title: Copenhagen International School Nordhavn
places.why: A school of four towers on a harbour peninsula covered in about 12,000 coloured solar panels, each set at its own angle so the façade shimmers in blue and green.

photos.file: Opening of the harbour bus stop Orientkaj Station 02.jpg
photos.author: Leif Jørgensen

places.title: Biblioteket Rentemestervej
places.why: A library, culture house and concert hall on one of the highest points of the city, built as four golden boxes stacked like books, with raw concrete walls inside covered in drawings by the artist HuskMitNavn.

places.title: Børnekulturhus Ama’r
places.why: One of the first culture houses designed for children, shaped with them in workshops. It fills a corner between two existing buildings and steps down to one storey at the corner to keep daylight in the courtyard behind.

places.title: Experimentarium
places.why: A science centre in a former bottling hall of the Tuborg brewery, rebuilt with a copper-clad helix staircase that winds through the building as its centrepiece.

places.title: Red Cross Volunteer House
places.why: A house for Red Cross volunteers by Trianglen whose roof and one wall are a giant yellow-brick staircase open to all, a public place to sit above the street.

places.title: Copenhagen Zoo: Elephant House and Panda House
places.why: In the zoo, two glass domes sunk into the slope shelter the elephants under a leaf-patterned canopy, and a yin-yang shaped garden house divides the two pandas.

places.title: Spidsen af Nordø (Tip of Nordø)
places.why: A 60-metre round office building at the entrance to the harbour, clad in angled panels of glass and galvanised steel that catch the sun like a lighthouse, around an atrium big enough to hold the Round Tower.

places.title: Kødbyen (Meatpacking District)
places.why: The city’s meat market, with the brick halls of the Brown Meat City and the white tiled functionalist halls of 1934, still partly used by the meat trade and filled with restaurants, bars and galleries.

places.title: Ørestad Gymnasium
places.why: A high school without classrooms in the usual sense: four boomerang-shaped floors rotate around a central atrium joined by a wide spiral stair, behind a façade of coloured glass louvres.

places.title: Carlsberg Byen and the Elephant Gate
places.why: The old Carlsberg brewery turned into a dense new district of narrow streets, keeping the brick brewhouses, the lighthouse-like chalk tower and the Elephant Gate, where four granite elephants carry a tower.

photos.author: Troels Dejgaard Hansen from Copenhagen, Denmark

places.title: CopenHill (Amager Bakke)
places.why: A waste-to-energy plant whose sloping roof is an artificial ski slope with a hiking trail and a climbing wall up the façade, a power station turned into a public mountain.

places.title: Den Blå Planet (National Aquarium)
places.why: The national aquarium, shaped like a whirlpool: aluminium-shingled arms spiral out from a central foyer, each leading to a different world of water.

places.title: Maritime Youth House
places.why: A sailing club and youth house on a polluted site where a timber deck rolls up and over the boat storage, making a wooden landscape of hills for play.

places.title: Kastrup Sea Bath
places.why: A circular wooden bathing pavilion on stilts at the end of a long pier, rising into a high diving tower and open to all for free.

photos.file: Kastrup Sea Bath and the Øresund Bridge - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: Jens Cederskjold

places.title: Cirkelbroen
places.why: A pedestrian and cycle bridge over the mouth of Christianshavn canal made of five circular platforms, each with a mast and cables like a ship, inviting people to stop over the water.

places.title: Cykelslangen (Bicycle Snake)
places.why: An orange-surfaced cycle bridge that winds above the harbourfront between buildings, lifting cyclists from the quay to the harbour bridge without stairs.

places.title: Lille Langebro
places.why: A swing bridge for cyclists and pedestrians of two curved steel arms that turn and meet over the harbour, slim enough to read as a line on the water.

places.title: Konditaget Lüders (Park ’n’ Play)
places.why: A red multi-storey car park in Nordhavn with a public playground and fitness park on its roof, 24 metres above the street, reached by two diagonal stairs on the façade among climbing plants.

places.title: Urban Rigger
places.why: Floating student housing made of stacked shipping containers on a pontoon, arranged around a sheltered courtyard on the water with a kayak landing.

places.title: 8 House (8Tallet)
places.why: A block of 475 homes shaped as a figure eight around two courtyards, with a sloping path you can cycle from the street to the tenth floor past terraced houses and gardens.

places.title: Mountain Dwellings (VM Bjerget)
places.why: Terraced flats with gardens stacked in a slope over a multi-storey car park, whose perforated aluminium façade shows a photograph of Mount Everest.

places.title: VM Houses
places.why: Two housing blocks in the shape of a V and an M, with triangular balconies sticking out like teeth and flats of many different types inside.

places.title: Tietgenkollegiet
places.why: A round student hall of residence around a courtyard, inspired by Chinese tulou houses, with rooms that jut out at different depths in copper and glass and shared kitchens facing inward.

photos.author: Peter Alfred Hess from United States

places.title: The Silo
places.why: A 1960s concrete grain silo turned into flats, wrapped in a new faceted skin of galvanised steel, with a public restaurant and terrace on top.

places.title: Krøyers Plads
places.why: Three brick housing blocks on the Christianshavn quay with folded roofs that echo the old warehouses next to them, and a stepped public waterfront.

places.title: Dortheavej Residence
places.why: Affordable social housing of prefabricated modules stacked in a checkerboard, every other one set back, with timber frames around tall windows; the middle of the block is pushed back to open a small plaza to the street.

places.title: Portland Towers
places.why: Two old cement silos in Nordhavn turned into offices: glass storeys are hung around and above the concrete cylinders, which stay visible inside.

places.title: Gemini Residence
places.why: Two concrete soybean silos on the harbour turned into flats by hanging the homes and balconies outside the cylinders and using their hollow cores as glass-roofed atriums.

photos.author: Tony Webster from Portland, Oregon, United States

places.title: Brumleby
places.architect: Michael Gottlieb Bindesbøll and Vilhelm Klein
places.why: Built after the cholera epidemic as healthy homes for workers: long yellow and white two-storey rows with gardens in between, one of the earliest social housing estates in Denmark.

places.title: Nyboder
places.why: Rows of low yellow terraced houses built for the navy’s sailors and their families, begun by Christian IV and still let to naval personnel.

places.title: Søholm
places.why: Terraced houses of yellow brick facing the sea, each with sloping roofs set at angles and a tall chimney, where Jacobsen lived and had his studio.

places.title: Tingbjerg and its library
places.architect: Steen Eiler Rasmussen and C.Th. Sørensen; COBE (library)
places.why: A post-war garden town of three-storey brick blocks set in green space, planned as a whole with shops and schools. Its new library and culture house, shared with the school, is a meeting place at the heart of the town.

places.title: Bispebjerg Bakke
places.architect: Bjørn Nørgaard with Henning Larsen Architects
places.why: Housing modelled in clay by the sculptor Bjørn Nørgaard: a red and yellow brick ribbon of three to eight storeys that winds over the slope like a dragon on stilts under a wavy copper roof.

places.title: Århusgadekvarteret, Nordhavn
places.why: The first finished quarter of the new Nordhavn district: converted silos and warehouses next to new blocks along narrow, sheltered streets, with a long waterside promenade and the Sandkaj harbour bath.

places.title: Superkilen
places.why: A 750-metre park through one of the most diverse neighbourhoods, in three parts: a red square for sport, a black square with white lines for sitting, and a green park. It holds objects from over 60 countries chosen by local residents.

places.title: Islands Brygge Harbour Bath
places.why: The first harbour bath, opened when the harbour water became clean enough to swim: timber decks and pools set into the canal, with diving towers, next to the lawns of Islands Brygge harbour park.

places.title: Kalvebod Waves
places.why: A wooden boardwalk that rises and dips over the harbour in front of an office quay, making room to sit, sunbathe and launch a kayak.

photos.author: Naotake Murayama from San Francisco, CA, USA

places.title: Frederiksberg Gardens, Frederiksberg Palace and Søndermarken
places.why: A romantic landscape garden of canals, islands, temples and a Chinese pavilion below the yellow baroque palace on the hill. Across the road, Søndermarken park hides the Cisterns, an old underground water reservoir.

places.title: Fælledparken
places.why: The city’s most used park, a former common with wide lawns, a lime avenue, themed flower gardens and a large open concrete skatepark.

places.title: Amager Strandpark
places.why: An artificial island with a long sandy beach and a lagoon, a short metro ride from the centre, with bathing piers, dunes and a promenade.

places.title: The Opera Park
places.why: A green front garden for the Opera on Dokøen, planted over a two-storey car park and arranged like a stage with foreground, middle ground and background, with plants that recall the ships trading with distant lands.

places.title: Sankt Kjelds Plads
places.why: A roundabout turned into a small urban forest that collects rainwater, with paths, hills and benches among wild planting where traffic used to circle.

places.title: Tåsinge Plads
places.why: The first climate-adapted square in Copenhagen: planted hollows store cloudburst water and inverted umbrellas pour rain into the beds, around a neighbourhood meeting place.

places.title: Grønningen-Bispeparken
places.why: A former grey lawn in a social housing estate turned into a climate park, where stormwater flows through basins that double as places to play and sit.

places.title: Enghaveparken
places.architect: Poul Holsøe; Arne Jacobsen (bandstand); Tredje Natur (renovation)
places.why: A neoclassical park of 1929 with a bandstand by the young Arne Jacobsen, renovated so that low walls and a sunken rose garden can hold the water of ten Olympic pools during cloudbursts.

places.title: Mariebjerg Cemetery
places.why: A modernist woodland cemetery divided into hedged rooms of different trees and plants, each with its own character, a landmark of Danish landscape architecture.

places.title: Guldbergs Plads
places.why: A neighbourhood square of grassy hills, poles and a small larch forest with wild flower meadows, used for play and a monthly farmers’ market.

places.title: Landbohøjskolens Have
places.why: The quiet teaching garden of the old agricultural college, with trees as old as the garden, a pond with an island, a rose garden and a greenhouse café; no ball games, bikes or dogs.

places.title: BaneGaarden
places.why: Nine wooden railway barns from the early 1900s, abandoned in the 1950s and overgrown, restored as a place for organic food and events while the wild nature around them was left untouched.

places.title: Karens Minde Aksen
places.why: A long green park in Sydhavn where a brick path winds like a river and guides cloudburst water over trickle meadows; playgrounds, dog runs and horse paddocks were kept at the residents’ request.

places.title: Remiseparken
places.why: The park of the Urbanplanen housing estate, renewed around a winding path of coloured concrete that widens into play areas and seats, with farm animals, kitchen gardens, a concrete skatepark and an alder wood.

places.title: Nørrebroparken
places.why: A long neighbourhood park on the line of an old railway, redesigned by Steen Høyer with football pitches, a skating rink and lawns between windbreaks of trees, linked to Superkilen.

places.title: Karen Blixens Plads
places.why: A university square whose grassy humps hide covered bicycle parking underneath, making a landscape of small hills to sit and lie on.
